item.title: Russia's Putin vows a response 'far more painful' after Ukraine attacks prized bridge in Crimea
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said I "believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did" to the Kerch Strait bridge this week.
item.content:encoded:
Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed Thursday to respond to Ukraine in a "far more painful" manner after Volodymyr Zelenskyy's forces heavily damaged the Kerch Strait bridge that has become a symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea.

The warning was issued as Ukraine's president said he arrived in Berlin, Germany for talks with more than 40 partners aimed at ending the war, including with President Donald Trump's son-in-law and advisor Jared Kushner and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff.

"We will respond to these strikes. And I want everyone to know this: I believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge," Putin said after meeting with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping for trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, according to Reuters.

"We will, of course, restore the bridge. The road section suffered serious damage," Putin reportedly added.

UKRAINE RELEASE VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE PUTIN'S PRIZE BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA

Ukraine attacked the bridge for the third time this week prior to Putin making his remarks, Reuters reported.

A Russian official told The Associated Press that the latest strike on the bridge linking Russia to Crimea halted rail traffic.

On Tuesday, the Security Service of Ukraine released videos showing the aftermath of a drone strike on the bridge, which destroyed one of its two arches and a roadway underneath it.

Putin said Thursday that he discussed with Russia's Security Council a potential stoppage of attacks at sea and against energy facilities, and "asked everyone to give it further thought and come back to it, hoping that perhaps some kind of agreement could be reached," according to Reuters.

"But after the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, there will be no agreements," Putin added.

TRUMP HISTORIC SUMMIT XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE

Zelenskyy has described the bridge as the "main military crossing from Russian territory into our Ukrainian Crimea."

Ahead of Thursday's Coalition of the Willing meeting in Germany, Zelenskyy said "Ukraine’s priorities are strengthening our air defense, energy and financial support, the diplomatic track, and the next steps toward ending the war and guaranteeing security.

"Bilateral meetings with European partners are also planned, and, of course, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. There will also be a format involving the American side and European national security advisors," he added.

Kushner said on X that the U.S. priorities for the trip "are to further strengthen our close coordination with Ukraine and Europe, work toward a unified position on the key elements of a lasting peace, and to jointly prepare the agenda and proposed format for the next round of multilateral negotiations."

Kushner declared that Trump is "determined to end this terrible war and create a lasting peace that makes all of Europe safer."

item.title: Hometown of accused US military plane saboteur is a known magnet for anti-Israel activism
item.description: Cork, Ireland, hometown of Daithí O’Corráin, who faces U.S. charges of destroying a $60 million C-130, once banned Benjamin Netanyahu from its city limits.
item.content:encoded:
The European hometown of the man who single-handedly destroyed a U.S. military transport aircraft in an act of apparent protest has a rich history of pro-Palestinian support.

This includes the town council for Cork, Ireland, barring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from entering its city limits, citing his "illegal occupation of Palestine and bordering countries" and the continuous pro-Palestinian protests taking place every Saturday since October 2023, organized by the Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign (CPSC).

Cork’s opposition to Israel adds context to the possible motives for why Daithí O’Corráin, an Irish national, allegedly destroyed a U.S. military C-130 Hercules aircraft in April. The incident also draws attention to several anti-Israel groups that have sprung up in Ireland in recent years.

IRELAND’S ELITES HAVE FOUND THEIR NEW RELIGION: HATING ISRAEL

Ireland’s anti-Israel foothold became international news in April when O’Corráin, a Cork native, barricaded himself inside a C-130, a U.S. military transport plane. Once inside, he tore out critical wiring, destroyed gauges, contaminated fuel tanks and even poured corrosive chemicals into the aircraft, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

Although his motives remain unclear, several groups from Cork interpreted his actions as a form of resistance against Israel and U.S. military interventionism.

In one such case, a Cork business owner named Tracey Ryan launched an initiative to raise €20,000 for O’Corráin's legal defense, praising his efforts to resist "the unwanted presence of U.S. military in Ireland in the face of their illegal war & support of Israel’s genocide."

"We, Daithí's friends and comrades, are raising funds to support him through his court case. We would really appreciate your support & will keep you updated here on ways to support Daithí," Ryan wrote in the description of the fundraising page.

According to her personal Facebook profile, Ryan joined a bus of pro-Palestinian activists who went to support O’Corráin at his court appearance. "Bus going to the high court to support Daithí on Thursday!!" Ryan wrote.

O’Corráin has also received support from CPSC, the Cork pro-Palestinian group.

As news of the incident spread, CPSC co-chair Anne McShane posted on her Palestinian advocacy Facebook page in support of O’Corráin, encouraging viewers to send him letters of encouragement after his incarceration.

"Daithi needs our support in order to keep up his morale. Letters are a lifeline for prisoners," an April 17 post read.

CPSC spearheads anti-Israel demonstrations in Cork. In addition to hosting several pro-Palestinian fundraising initiatives, the group facilitates weekly Saturday demonstrations and invites speakers. At one point, CPSC’s website featured a fundraising site for O’Corráin, but the page has since been removed.

INSIDE THE PROTEST PLAYBOOK TO VILIFY ISRAEL ON 'GLOBAL DAY OF ACTION'

In CPSC’s own words, the group is part of a larger pro-Palestinian movement.

"It’s not just the city. Towns across all of County Cork stand in solidarity with Palestinians, including Ballincollig, Bandon, Cobh, Charleville, Clonakilty, Fermoy, Kinsale, Macroom, Mallow, Mitchelstown, Skibbereen and more," the group states on its website.

"Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign is a branch of the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign (IPSC)," it added.

As part of its sister groups’ efforts "to foster links between Palestine and Irish institutions and organizations," CPSC and IPSC have both applauded Cork’s city council efforts to promote pro-Palestinian policies.

"Well done to the Cork City Council which passed a motion … calling for the Central Bank to end the sale of Israeli bonds," one Facebook post reads.

The groups have also held Cork up as a template for Ireland’s national policy.

"We call on the Irish government to follow the example of both Dublin and Cork city councils by officially recognizing Israeli Apartheid – and acting to end any and all links to this regime," another statement reads.

For its own part, the Cork City Council has earned the support of IPSC and CPSC through a range of its official resolutions, making the town’s formal position to condemn any of Ireland’s ties to Israel.

In addition to banning Netanyahu from entering the city's limits in a 41-8 vote in 2024, Cork’s council has flown the Palestinian flag over city hall on U.N. International Day of Solidarity and called on Ireland to ban trade from Israeli settlements.

Cork has even passed a "twinning" mechanism with the Palestinian city of Nablus — a largely symbolic partnership.

IRISH PM REJECTS ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS IN IRELAND AMID DRAMATIC VOTE OVER BOYCOTTING ISRAEL GAME

Fergal Dennehy, the lord mayor of Cork from 2025 to 2026, hosted the mayor of Nablus in February, calling the partnership "just the beginning of what we hope will be a wonderful relationship between our two great cities."

Neither CPSC nor Cork City Council responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment on the city's pro-Palestinian positions or about connections to O’Corráin.

O’Corráin is incarcerated in Ireland and faces criminal charges in the U.S. for "destruction of government property," valued at $60 million.

Somewhere between Sunday and Thursday, the betting market decided the Houston Texans are a juggernaut.

The Texans opened as 10-point favorites against Indianapolis. Now they’re laying 12.5. That’s nearly a three-point move in favor of a 3-6 team that just blew a 17-0 lead to Cleveland, has one win all year over a team with more than one victory and hasn’t covered a single game at home.

I don’t buy it. This line moved for the wrong reasons, and that’s where the value is. Now the Texans welcome the Colts on TNF in a divisional matchup.

Start with the Texans’ résumé as a favorite. They’re 3-6 against the spread overall, 2-5 as a favorite and 0-4 against the spread at home. Laying double digits with this team requires believing it’s about to become something it hasn’t been all season.

Last week was the clearest example. Houston led Cleveland 17-0 and lost. Stroud threw 38 times for just 211 yards. In the first meeting with Indianapolis, which the Colts won, he threw for 167 yards and one touchdown.

The injury report doesn’t help Houston, either. Danielle Hunter, the Texans’ best pass rusher, is out with a hamstring injury. So are Marvin Harrison Jr. and running back Woody Marks. David Montgomery is playing through a groin injury on a short week, and Azeez Al-Shaair, Houston’s leading tackler, is on injured reserve.

That doesn’t add up to a team that should be winning by two touchdowns.

The Colts are 3-7, so I’m not here to sell you on them as a good team. I’m here to sell you on 12.5 points.

Indianapolis has covered in seven straight trips to Houston as a road underdog, and it’s 2-2 against the spread on the road this season. Divisional road underdogs are 16-12 against the spread this year, and favorites laying seven or more are just 15-19-2.

Thursday nights also tend to stay closer than expected. Underdogs are 6-4 against the spread on Thursday nights this season, and short weeks favor whichever team can run the ball and shorten the game.

The money backs it up. When the public pushes a line up three points and the bigger money goes the other way, I know which side I want.

The concern is real, though. Indy is banged up on the offensive line, with left tackle Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis both out. In the Week 3 meeting, Daniel Jones was pressured on 19 of 41 dropbacks and committed three turnovers under pressure. Without Hunter, Houston’s ability to repeat that takes a big hit.

Houston ranks 20th in EPA per rush and allows 4.0 yards per carry. Taylor cleared this number against the Texans in Week 3 on 23 carries.

The snap count is the one worry. Taylor has played under 70% of the offensive snaps in four straight games, with rookie Seth McGowan taking some work. But Taylor still gets the volume, and a game script where Indianapolis is trying to keep it close favors the ground game.

The Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the deadline, and those targets have to go somewhere. Warren is the answer. I loved Warren preseason and it feels like the Colts have neglected him, so now is the time for one of the best young tight ends in football to break out.

He had nine catches against Houston in Week 3 and has caught at least five passes in each of his last two games against the Texans. With Brevin Jordan out for Houston and the Colts likely leaning on quick, short throws to protect a battered offensive line, the tight end becomes Jones’s first read.

item.title: Rob Lowe calls out Hollywood double standard after festivals reject Ben Shapiro-written film
item.description: Rob Lowe said on The Free Press podcast that festivals rejected his Ben Shapiro film "Confession" over politics, and a critic warned he could "pay a professional price."
item.content:encoded:
Actor Rob Lowe is calling out what he describes as the entertainment industry’s political double standard, suggesting his new movie struggled to secure major film festival screenings because it was written by conservative commentator Ben Shapiro.

Speaking on The Free Press’ "Second Thought" podcast, "The West Wing" alum said major distributors showed little interest in his historical drama "Confession," despite a cast that includes Nick Nolte, James Franco and Jennifer Jason Leigh.

"We got turned down by every single film festival," Lowe said. "Summarily frog-marched out of any conversation. Now this is a movie with me, Nick Nolte, James Franco, Emile Hirsch. I see what they’re picking up and it’s all political."

KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE

The feature film was written by conservative commentator Ben Shapiro, whose media company, The Daily Wire, is distributing the movie after Lowe said other distributors passed on it. Set during Josef Stalin’s Great Purge, the drama stars Lowe as a Soviet prisoner and holds a 91% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes as of Thursday.

When a podcast host pointed out the irony of a movie about Soviet "wrongthink" facing political pushback in modern-day Hollywood, Lowe agreed, calling it "the greatest irony."

KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS

"A lot of people cannot see a work just for its work. They have to do the math of what does it mean and what will people think and does that mean I’m on this side or does that mean I’m on that side?" Lowe said.

Lowe said he called Shapiro to praise the script after reading it, prompting The Daily Wire co-founder to ask if he knew any leading men in their 50s "who would not be scared just because I wrote it."

GLEN POWELL WANTS NO PART OF POLITICAL FIGHTS THAT DIVIDE PEOPLE

"And I go, ‘Yeah, me.’ And he goes, ‘You’re good with this?’" Lowe recalled. "I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’"

Lowe added, "The thought would be we’d play in a film festival, we would get some buzz—never happened. And then, you know, Netflix would pick it up or this one would pick [it up]—crickets. Absolute crickets."

He continued, "So then it defaults to The Daily Wire to be the distributor, and I’m like, ‘Hell yeah!’ I want people to see this movie."

"Confession" premiered at the Warsaw Film Festival in October, according to published reports.

Fox News Digital reached out to Netflix for comment. 

Entertainment critic Christian Toto said Lowe could "pay a professional price" for appearing in the film, despite his long career in Hollywood.

"Rob Lowe got a crash course in how conservatives are treated in Hollywood. He isn't an ideologue, nor does he speak out on political issues regularly. The simple act of starring in a film written by a conservative puts a target on his back, and that's something no actor wants," Toto, editor of the Hollywood in Toto website, told Fox News Digital.

"Kudos to Lowe for being forthright about his views on the subject, and for putting the art above any tribal allegiances. Sadly, he may still pay a professional price for appearing in ‘Confession,’" he added.

item.title: Florida DMV worker faces 360 felonies for allegedly helping illegal aliens get licenses without driving tests
item.description: Investigators say Lynnette Stitt Williams accepted fake utility bills and skipped driving tests to push 60 licenses through Pembroke Pines office.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida driver's license examiner faces 360 felony charges after investigators say she accepted fake utility bills and bypassed mandatory driving tests to help dozens of unqualified applicants — including illegal aliens — obtain state driver's licenses.

According to court documents, 56-year-old Lynnette Stitt Williams, of Miami, was arrested Monday and hit with six separate third-degree felonies for each of the 60 licenses she allegedly helped push through at the Pembroke Pines driver's license office – including forgery, official misconduct, falsifying public records and unlawfully issuing driver's licenses.

The investigation was sparked after an attorney representing several people who paid for licenses emailed the Florida Highway Patrol's Bureau of Criminal Investigations and Intelligence.

WOMAN EXPOSED RUNNING VISA FRAUD SCHEME SPANNING YEARS, POSING AS IMMIGRATION OFFICER

Troopers learned that a man posing as an immigration attorney had arranged their exams through First Driving School Corp. and gave them Williams as a direct point of contact inside the Pembroke Pines office.

"Applicants would pay a set fee to said driving school, and it guarantees obtaining a driver's license regardless of legal status or other unqualified circumstances," troopers wrote in the arrest report.

BODYCAM VIDEO SHOWS CANADIAN WOMAN ALLEGEDLY GIVING FALSE NAME BEFORE DEPUTIES DISCOVERED 12 FAKE IDS

When Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles compliance examiners audited Williams's 2024 and 2025 transactions — before she transferred to a tax collector's office — they uncovered a widespread pattern of fake proof-of-residency paperwork.

Investigators allegedly found fake utility, cable and insurance bills that recycled the exact same account, invoice or membership numbers across completely different applicants, alongside altered bills with missing street numbers or containing obvious typos like "31days."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The audit also flagged additional driving schools in Williams's transaction history, including one where applicants repeatedly listed the business owner's personal home as their address.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Troopers allege Williams personally signed forms falsely claiming that multiple applicants all lived at the home of a "Mr. Hugo," who was tied to a driving school funneling applicants directly to her.

"Considered together, these circumstances support an inference of knowing participation rather than an isolated document-review error," the report states.

GOT A TIP?

Beyond rubber-stamping bogus residency records, investigators say Williams allowed referred applicants to skip the standard appointment line, repeatedly processed the same customers and upgraded learner's permits to replacement licenses on the same day.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

She also allegedly waived mandatory in-office written and driving re-tests for applicants who had been flagged to retake their exams.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

After reviewing the case with prosecutors, troopers staked out Williams's Miami home early Monday morning. They watched her leave for her job at the tax collector's office around 7:20 a.m., pulled her over eight minutes later and booked her into the Broward County jail.

Following the arrest, Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia — posting from his X account — announced he had coordinated with state licensing officials to cancel the fraudulent licenses. "CONFIRMED," Ingoglia wrote. "All the licenses given to illegals have been REVOKED."

item.title: Police called to Chargers QB Justin Herbert's fiancée Madison Beer's home for possible burglary
item.description: Madison Beer's Hollywood Hills home drew a police response over a reported prowler on security camera, with two masked men spotted near a white SUV.
item.content:encoded:
Police were called to the Hollywood Hills home of singer Madison Beer — fiancée of Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert — on Wednesday evening after reports of a possible burglary.

According to The New York Post, police received a call at 7:56 p.m. local time about a possible burglary and two men wearing dark clothing and facemasks in the neighborhood outside of Beer's home.

The reports also claim that the two suspects carried large backpacks and were driving a white SUV. However, when police arrived on the scene, they did not find any signs that a burglary had occurred.

ACTRESS MONET MAZUR'S $1.5M HOLLYWOOD HILLS HOME TARGETED BY MASKED SUSPECTS IN BREAK-IN ATTEMPT

It remains unclear whether Beer or Herbert was in the home at the time the call came in, though Los Angeles TV station ABC7 shared video that appears to show the singer and the Chargers quarterback speaking to police outside the home.

TMZ reports that the initial call came after someone spotted a prowler on their security camera.

Purchased in 2022, Beer’s three-bedroom, four-bath home is worth an estimated $5.5 million.

CHARGERS QUARTERBACK JUSTIN HERBERT AND POP STAR MADISON BEER ANNOUNCE ENGAGEMENT WITH ROMANTIC POST

Herbert is coming off his and the Chargers' first win of the season, which happened on Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens. The victory snapped an 11-game losing streak for the team.

This incident comes as there has been a rash of break-ins and burglaries targeting homes tied to professional athletes.

Earlier this year, Chilean nationals wanted in connection with burglaries at the homes of Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, as well as Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and Bobby Portis of the Miami Heat, were arrested in Argentina.

Additionally, earlier in the week, US Open champ Sloane Stephens’ home in Sherman Oaks, California, was also broken into, though the suspects fled. Three suspects were arrested later in the evening.

item.title: 12-year-old Little League baseball player succumbs to injury, dies after being in months-long coma
item.description: Xavier Taylor, a 12-year-old New Jersey boy struck by a baseball in May, died Wednesday after cardiac arrest and a medically induced coma, per reports.
item.content:encoded:
A story involving a young boy from New Jersey fighting for his life following a baseball injury has taken a tragic turn.

Xavier Taylor, a 12-year-old from Maple Shade, NJ, died Wednesday after being placed in a coma, according to a local FOX affiliate.

Taylor was struck in the neck by a baseball while warming up for a game back in May of this year.

HIGH SCHOOL LACROSSE PLAYER DIES AFTER ROUTINE PLAY TURNS FATAL, SECOND SUCH DEATH IN A YEAR

The injury led to cardiac arrest, and he was eventually placed in a medically induced coma.

His community banded together during this time to offer as much support as they possibly could, holding vigils and fundraising money for Taylor's family.

Baseball teams in his league even wore special patches in his honor, and churches nationwide even held prayer groups for Taylor.

WE ARE LOOKING AT YOUTH SPORTS ALL WRONG AND THAT CAN LEAD TO INJURIES AND BURNOUT

Sarah Diphillipo, a vigil coordinator, said, "We are here because we are believing God for a miracle for Xavier, but we are also believing for a move of God throughout our entire community and nation."

The Maple Shade Youth Baseball league released a statement regarding Taylor's passing.

"Over these past six months, we have watched something truly incredible happen. A community, and people from all over the country, came together for one boy and his family. We have seen blue lights shine, bats displayed, shirts worn, fundraisers organized, donations poured in, and countless prayers lifted," they wrote.

"Xavier was one of our own, and this loss will forever leave a hole in our baseball community."

"Xavier loves baseball, he loves our community and he loves Jesus and he would be so happy to see everyone supporting him," said Gregory Taylor, Xavier's father, before his passing.

The tragedy has struck the local community particularly hard, with the Maple Shade Youth Baseball league encouraging counseling for those affected.

item.content:encoded:
The cast of "Landman" is growing.

The popular series created by Taylor Sheridan focuses on the oil business in Texas, and it's been an entertainment monster through its first two seasons.

One of the reasons the show is such a draw is that it features a cast with star power rarely seen on TV. That includes Billy Bob Thornton, Ali Larter, Demi Moore, Sam Elliott, Michelle Randolph, Jacob Lofland and Jon Hamm (season one only).

Deadline reported Wednesday that actor Scott Speedman is joining the cast for season three of the series.

Deadline reported that "details regarding his character are under wraps" for the time being. Production is also already underway on the upcoming third season.

Speedman has a long and very successful acting career. He's appeared in "R.J. Decker," "Animal Kingdom," "Grey's Anatomy" and many other notable projects.

My personal favorite is "Last Resort." While the show didn't last long and wasn't particularly great TV, it was incredibly entertaining.

item.title: Mike Florio issues weak one-sentence apology for Hitler joke about Mike Vrabel's mustache after NFL's rebuke
item.description: Mike Florio and Chris Simms apologized for their Mike Vrabel mustache joke during trip to Germany that the NFL called inappropriate and offensive.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL did not find Mike Florio and Chris Simms joking about New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel's mustache apparently resembling Adolf Hitler’s all that funny. However, the well-known on-air hosts don't appear too concerned about the league's opinion on the matter.

During Tuesday's edition of "PFT Live," Florio and Simms shared a back-and-forth about Vrabel drinking a beer in Germany ahead of the Patriots' matchup against the Detroit Lions last Sunday in Munich, putting focus on the coach's facial hair.

After Simms stated that Vrabel had "the German mustache," Florio responded by stating, "If you're in Germany, you've got to be careful trimming that thing." After sharing that the show's producer, Gary Carter, was "groaning" about the statement, Florio went on to say, "It's funny, Gary, it was 80 years ago, let us have some fun."

MIKE FLORIO SAYS HITLER JOKE ABOUT MIKE VRABEL MUSTACHE IS OK BECAUSE IT'S BEEN 80 YEARS | BOBBY BURACK

Neither Florio nor Simms said Hitler's name during the exchange on the show, although it seems quite clear they were alluding to the former leader of the Nazi Party and the Holocaust.

Jeff Miller, the NFL's executive vice president of communications and public affairs, said in a statement that the league "found the remarks inappropriate and offensive," according to the New York Post.

MIKE FLORIO ENDS 'CONSCIOUS VOTING PROTEST,' DECIDES TO VOTE IN 2026 MIDTERMS

Florio and Simms issued a one-sentence apology that was shared on the NBC Sports website on Wednesday: "On yesterday’s (Nov. 17) 'PFT Live' show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize."

Florio is the founder of "Pro Football Talk" and has been a longtime NFL analyst with NBC Sports, which distributes the show across Peacock and NBC Sports NOW. NBC Sports has been a primetime broadcast partner with the NFL since 2006 with "Sunday Night Football."

In September, Florio opined that the New York Giants should sign Colin Kaepernick after quarterback Jaxson Dart was ruled out for the season after suffering an injury. Kaepernick, 39, has not taken a snap in the NFL since the 2016 season.

item.description: Syria's top Christian leaders warn that escalating attacks, kidnappings and violence threaten their community's future, as the State Department voices concern over religious persecution.
item.content:encoded:
The leaders of Syria’s oldest Christian denominations issued a dire warning about the intensified persecution of their communities and whether there is a future for them in the Middle Eastern nation.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, a former U.S.-designated terrorist who commanded the al Qaeda-linked Nusra Front during the nation's civil war, has since sought to distance himself from his extremist past as he oversees the nation's rebuilding amid a deteriorating situation for Christians and other minorities.

Senior Christians released a joint statement that noted "a series of heinous and recurring attacks targeting the Syrian people, and Christians in particular. Time and again, we have raised our voices, and we continue to do so, as this wave of attacks has persisted without interruption. These attacks are not, and have never been, isolated incidents." 

The signers were John X, Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East, Ignatius Aphrem II, Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East, and Youssef Absi, Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarch of Antioch and All the East.

SYRIA OFF US TERROR BLACKLIST AFTER NEARLY 50 YEARS AS TRUMP ADMIN CLEARS INVESTMENT HURDLE

The religious leaders cited examples of recent violent attacks on members of the Christian community in the Muslim-majority country.

"What has happened, and continues to happen, in many places, including most recently in Al- Suqaylabiyah, in the form of systematic assaults and kidnappings carried out for exorbitant ransom payments, constitutes a violation of the most basic human rights, as evidenced by the video showing the brutal torture of the jeweler Maher Sankari," they wrote.

"In view of the competent authorities' failure to provide security and protection in response to what has occurred and continues to occur, these attacks have once again escalated in recent days, culminating in the targeting of Archbishop Youhanna Abdo Arbash of the Melkite Greek Catholic Archdiocese of Homs, Hama, Al-Nabk Yabroud, and their Dependencies. He was bound, blindfolded, and gagged while his office was ransacked. "

The leaders warned about a "grave question regarding the future of Christians in this country."

TURKEY DEPORTS PEACEFUL CHRISTIANS UNDER GUISE OF 'NATIONAL SECURITY' CLAIMS WATCHDOG

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "We are concerned by reports of attacks, kidnappings and violence against Christians in Syria and regularly raise these concerns with the Syrian government. We continue to stress the importance of protecting the unalienable rights of all Syrians, regardless of ethnicity or religion."

Alberto Fernandez, former U.S. ambassador and Mideast analyst, who closely follows the persecution of Christians in the region, told Fox News Digital, "The government in Damascus is an Islamist-controlled one but has tried generally to treat Christians fairly — more so than the treatment of Alawites and Druze. So some Christian property has been returned and some Christian representation has been secured. The regime is still deeply ideological, and includes figures that are more extreme than the norm. "

He added, "Christian existence is seen more as a concession than a question of fundamental rights. But the biggest danger for Christians has been the government's inability to secure law and order in the country, especially in some areas like Homs, and the difficulty in improving the country's disastrous economic situation. So deep economic crisis and crime/chaos have driven Christian flight more than actual persecution by the state. "

Fox News Digital reported last year about radical Islamists who targeted Syrian Christians and reportedly murdered Khaled Mazhar, pastor of the Good Shepherd Evangelical Church in Sweida, along with 11 family members. An additional person survived the massacre of Christians because the Islamists thought she was dead.

CHRISTIAN-JEWISH ORGANIZATION DELIVERS EMERGENCY AID TO PERCECUTED SYRIAN MINORITIES UNDER THREAT

While the Syrian government did not respond to Fox News Digital requests for comment, there have been some positive pronouncements over the last year, according to reports. After the bombing of the Mar Elias Church in Damascus last year, when the Islamic State murdered 25 people, President al-Sharaa pledged to tackle security threats against Christians.

In 2025, his government said it prevented a planned attack on a church in Tartus. Syria’s Interior Ministry said two men had been arrested "en route to carry out a terrorist operation." 

Syria appointed Hind Kabawat, a lawyer, as minister of social affairs and labor. She is the only Christian and woman in the president's cabinet. 

A British government report from earlier this year seemed to downplay threats to the Christian community. It noted, in part, "Since coming to power in Dec. 2024, the new government has engaged with Christian and Shia community leaders and has provided security for religious sites and festivals. While there are reports of attacks, harassment and discrimination by both state and non-state actors, the frequency and severity of these incidents do not suggest that there is a generalized risk to Christians and Shia Muslims."

Yet the Rev. Dr. Petra Heltd, a Christian scholar, told Fox News Digital, "The Joint Statement issued regarding the escalating wave of violence, extortion, and targeted attacks against the Christian communities in Syria is a heartfelt cry for help. "

She said, "While standing in solidarity with the suffering brothers and sisters in Syria, we call upon international governments, diplomatic missions and multilateral bodies to take concrete steps to support and protect Christians in Syria and to speak out against those acts against the ancient, living Christian presence in the region — a community that has already dwindled from only roughly one million before 2011 to fewer than 300,000 today."

STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION

Hayvi Bouzo, who was born in Syria and is the co-founder and executive director of Middle East 24, told Fox News Digital, "Kidnappings for ransom, an assault on a bishop, and repeated attacks on Christians are not isolated incidents. They are a pattern, and they show that extremist Islamist elements still operate with impunity in parts of Syria. That is not the new Syria that can be stable. Given America’s involvement in Syria, Washington has both the leverage and the responsibility to make the protection of minorities a clear, stated pillar of U.S. policy, and to ensure these abuses do not go unpunished."

Israel’s special envoy to the Christian world, George Deek, told Fox News Digital, "The latest warning from Syria’s church leaders clearly shows that a regime that emerged from jihadist movements and continues to rely on fighters from that background offers little reassurance to Christians or other minorities. We have already seen the consequences for the Druze and Alawites. This is a recurring pattern that should alarm everyone."

He added, "The international community must stop mistaking promises of moderation for actual moderation. Any engagement with Damascus must be conditioned on concrete protection for minorities, accountability for perpetrators and genuine religious freedom. The future of Syria’s ancient Christian communities cannot depend on the goodwill of former jihadists."

item.title: Apple Photos AI watermark can tag your real pictures
item.description: Apple Photos now embeds an invisible SynthID watermark in images edited with Apple Intelligence tools like Clean Up, Extend and Reframe in iOS 27.2.
item.content:encoded:
You take a great family photo, but there's one problem. Someone you don't know walked into the background. So you open Apple Photos, use Clean Up to remove the person and save your picture. Problem solved, right? Well, there's something new happening behind the scenes.

With iOS 27.2, Apple Photos can now add an invisible AI watermark to pictures you edit using certain Apple Intelligence tools. You won't see it on your screen. And if you share the photo, the person receiving it probably won't notice anything different either. But the watermark could still be there.

Apple introduced the feature in its Oct. 26 update. It uses Google's SynthID technology to identify images created or modified with artificial intelligence. Even a photo you took yourself can receive this hidden marker after certain AI edits. So how does it work, and what does it mean for the photos you share?

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

STOP LOSING PHOTO QUALITY WHEN YOU SHARE PICTURES

AI photo editing has come a long way. What once required complicated software can now take a few taps on your phone. That's convenient when you want to improve a picture. However, it also makes it harder to tell what's real. Someone can remove an important detail from a photo without leaving an obvious trace. AI can even generate parts of a scene that the camera never captured.

Apple's new watermarking feature gives people a way to tell when AI has been used to create or change an image. According to Apple's official support documentation, certain Apple Intelligence tools now add a hidden SynthID watermark when you create or edit images.

SynthID is technology developed by Google. It embeds a digital signal into an image that compatible detection tools can recognize. The watermark doesn't visibly change your photo. There's no stamp across the bottom or warning in the corner. Instead, the marker remains hidden unless someone checks the image with a SynthID detector.

Apple says the feature applies to certain Apple Intelligence tools starting with iOS 27.2. Here's where you might encounter it.

Clean Up lets you erase distractions from your pictures. Maybe someone wandered into your vacation photo. Or perhaps there's an object in the background you wish you could remove. You can use Clean Up to erase that distraction while AI fills in the missing area. With iOS 27.2, some photos edited this way can receive a SynthID watermark. However, Apple doesn't say that every small edit will trigger one. The watermark can depend on the changes made to the image.

Have you ever taken a picture and realized you were standing too close? Apple's Extend tool can help by generating additional scenery beyond the original edges of your photo. For example, you might have cropped out part of a building. Extend can generate additional background to make the composition look better. The result may look like you captured a wider shot in the first place. However, because AI creates part of the finished image, the photo can receive a hidden SynthID watermark. We've previously explained how Extend works in our article on fixing badly framed photos after you take them.

Apple also includes Spatial Reframing, called Reframe in Photos, among the tools covered by SynthID. Reframe lets you change the apparent perspective of a picture after you've taken it. You can adjust the angle or shift the composition while Apple Intelligence generates the necessary visual information. That can make a photo look quite different from what your camera originally captured. And because AI helps create that result, the edited image may carry a watermark.

Apple's watermarking feature also covers images generated using Image Playground and Image Wand. Image Playground lets you create images with AI using descriptions or other visual inputs. Image Wand can turn a rough sketch into a more developed image. Since these tools generate visual content, their inclusion makes sense. But Apple's decision to mark certain edits to genuine photos raises a more interesting question. Should a real photo receive an AI marker because you removed one distracting object?

NEW YORK MAKES HISTORY WITH FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND LAW REGULATING AI-POWERED COMMERCIALS

You might be wondering whether there's an easy way to see if a photo contains one of these hidden markers. There is, although you'll need to use an online detector. Apple recommends Google's SynthID Detector, which can analyze an uploaded image for the watermark.

One thing to understand: finding a watermark doesn't automatically mean a photo is fake. It simply indicates that AI was involved in creating or modifying the image. And the reverse is also true. If no watermark appears, that doesn't prove the picture is genuine. Other AI image generators may not use SynthID. Detection can also have limitations. I would also be careful about uploading private family pictures or sensitive images to any online service. Review how the service handles uploaded files before submitting them.

Apple says photos created or edited before the 27.2 update won't automatically receive a new SynthID watermark from Apple. So you don't have to worry about the update going through your entire photo library and adding markers to everything.

However, that changes if you open an older picture and edit it using one of the supported AI tools. For example, you could take a photo from five years ago and use Extend to improve the framing today. The newly edited version may then receive the invisible watermark.

Apple has also expanded this feature beyond iPhones. According to the company, SynthID support begins with these software versions: iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 and visionOS 27.2. Keep in mind that the software update and Apple Intelligence have different device requirements.

OPENAI CHILD SAFETY TOOLS TARGET AI-GENERATED ABUSE

You'll need an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone to use the editing features that trigger these watermarks. Apple Intelligence works on the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max, along with iPhone 16 models and newer compatible iPhones. The standard iPhone 15 can install iOS 27.2, but it doesn't support these Apple Intelligence editing features. Availability may also depend on your region and language.

To check for the latest software update:

I like the idea of giving people another way to question what they're seeing online. But there's an important limitation. Let's say you use Clean Up to remove someone standing behind your family in a vacation photo. Now compare that with an AI-generated picture showing an event that never happened. Both images could carry SynthID watermarks, even though the circumstances are very different.

The detector may identify AI involvement. However, it won't necessarily explain what was changed or how significant those changes were. That's a pretty big limitation when you're trying to decide whether to trust an image.

There's also the issue of AI-generated pictures that have no detectable watermark. So, while SynthID can provide a useful clue, it shouldn't be your only way of evaluating a suspicious photo. If a picture online seems questionable, look for the original source. You can also use a reverse image search to see where a photo originally appeared and whether earlier versions exist.

I can see why Apple is doing this. AI has gotten so good at changing photos that it's becoming harder to know what you're actually looking at. And I think that's a real concern. At the same time, I like having tools that can fix a great picture when someone walks into the background. Why should that photo get the same kind of watermark as a picture created entirely by AI? That's where I think Apple could do better. I'd love to see a way to check a photo and find out exactly what AI changed. Was it something minor, or did someone completely alter what happened? That's what I'd want to know before deciding whether to trust what I'm seeing.

Should Apple put a hidden AI watermark on your personal photos simply because you removed something from the background? Or should these markers be reserved for images that AI creates entirely? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Iowa residents near ammunition plant told to vacate before Army detonates 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals
item.description: The Army asked Middletown, Iowa, residents to temporarily evacuate Friday before it detonates 68 drums of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant.
item.content:encoded:
The Army is asking residents of a southeast Iowa town to temporarily evacuate Friday as it plans to detonate five tons of a bomb-making chemical that it says has turned into an "explosive safety hazard" after being "deemed unsafe for relocation."

It warned that the detonation of the 68 drums of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown "will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground." Lead azide is a chemical that is used to set off munitions.

"While safety measures will be fully enforced, the controlled detonation will cause temporary noise, ground vibrations, and a dust plume that will contain some lead," according to the Army. "Residents in Middletown will hear a loud noise; feel vibrations from two consecutive, rapid detonations; and see a plume of dust which is expected to linger for no more than one hour after the detonation, depending on wind speed."

Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but there are thousands more in the track of the plume, prompting a notification to communities as far as 100 miles away.

CRIMINAL PAST OF ILLINOIS ETHANOL PLANT BOMB SCARE SUSPECT INCLUDES MULTIPLE FELONIES, 2 PRISON STINTS

Middletown residents learned in March that the Army needed to dispose of several dozen barrels containing lead azide, after the ammunition plant paused operations as part of a review and the degraded material was discovered.

"The safety of our people and our neighbors is non‑negotiable," Lt. Col. Daniel Nosse, commander of the plant, said at the time.

The Army shared more details during a public meeting in Middletown in October, advising that a detonation was planned for an unspecified date in November. On Nov. 13, the Environmental Protection Agency approved an emergency permit, paving the way for Friday's detonation.

"EPA issued the Emergency Permit based upon the determination that the explosion risk from the degraded condition of the lead azide presented an imminent and substantial threat to human health and the environment," the EPA said.

"The Army has provided EPA information documenting that recrystallization of the lead azide in long-term storage has occurred. The recrystallization of lead azide has created a risk of spontaneous explosion due to the material’s sensitivity to friction and shock, creating a highly unstable and dangerous situation," according to the EPA.

LIVE WWII-ERA GRENADES TURN UP IN UNLIKELY PLACE; BOMB SQUAD WARNS OF DANGER

"The Army, which has unparalleled expertise in matters concerning explosives safety, concluded that this material cannot safely be handled or moved and therefore, cannot be treated by any method other than in-place detonation," it also said.

The Army said that the lead azide barrels "will be detonated inside earth-covered magazines made of concrete, and surrounded with Hesco barriers full of sand which are approximately two stories high."

Residents of Middletown are being advised to leave their homes between 8 a.m. and 2 p.m. local time Friday.

Officials also have released maps showing the potential for lead dust to drift north toward other communities. Some schools in the path of the plume have canceled classes.

"Before and during the detonation, the soil above the earth-covered magazines will be thoroughly saturated with water, and water misters will be spraying. These measures should reduce the amount of lead that migrates from the detonation through the air off the installation," the Army said. "Extensive modeling efforts predict that the potential level of lead particles in the air may be elevated but well below the level at which EPA would require protective actions be taken."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: AOC leaves door open to 2028 presidential run, signals willingness to work with Trump
item.description: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez would not rule out a 2028 White House run, saying her focus is getting results for people after Democrats reclaimed the House majority.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is leaving the door open to a potential 2028 presidential bid as speculation grows over her political future.

"I think, right now, this election just happened. We got to work on getting results for people," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital when asked whether she was considering a presidential run in 2028.

The self-described democratic socialist also expressed a willingness to work with President Donald Trump on key legislative priorities as Democrats prepare to take control of the House following the 2026 midterm elections.

PROGRESSIVE ORG LAUNCHES CAMPAIGN URGING AOC TO RUN FOR PRESIDENT WHILE PROGRESSIVES EYE SOCIALIST CANDIDATE

Ocasio-Cortez, who has drawn support from the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) New York City chapter for a potential White House bid, emphasized her desire to advance legislation in the 120th Congress rather than focus on presidential politics.

Asked whether Democrats should work with Trump instead of prioritizing impeachment proceedings and congressional investigations, Ocasio-Cortez expressed optimism about finding common ground.

"I hope so," she told Fox News Digital.

"You know, I hope that President Trump can sign a congressional stock trading ban into law," Ocasio-Cortez continued.

The congresswoman also identified healthcare reform as a potential area for bipartisan cooperation, urging Trump to address changes to Medicaid that she warned could threaten coverage for millions of Americans.

DOZENS OF HOUSE DEMOCRATS REJECT BILL FUSING CONGRESSIONAL STOCK BAN WITH FEDERAL VOTER ID

"I hope President Trump will be willing to work with us in really adjusting this Medicaid and confronting this Medicaid cliff that stands to kick off millions of working Americans off of their healthcare," she said.

"And so, you know, there are going to be areas where we're going to have real disagreement and real confrontation or worse," she continued.

Despite those disagreements, Ocasio-Cortez argued that lawmakers should prioritize legislation addressing Americans' immediate concerns.

"My hope is that we can prioritize the things that can actually change people's lives for the better as quickly as possible," she said.

Her remarks came hours after House Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., for speaker of the 120th Congress.

At least five of the 11 Democrats who opposed Jeffries’ nomination are incoming Congress members and self-described democratic socialists who argued that the party's leadership does not adequately represent their political priorities.

JEFFRIES SURVIVES DEM VOTE TO SECURE SPEAKER POSITION AS PROGRESSIVE RESISTANCE CLOUDS HIS CHANCES

Ocasio-Cortez, a DSA member, acknowledged that ideological disagreements between Jeffries and the party's socialist wing could continue throughout the next Congress.

"Of course, there are going to be areas where leader Jeffries and DSA are going to be in strong opposition," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital.

However, she expressed confidence that Democrats could unite around shared priorities, including expanding access to publicly funded healthcare.

Her comments highlight the competing pressures facing House Democrats as they prepare to govern with a new majority while balancing progressive policy demands, internal ideological divisions and potential opportunities to work with the Trump administration.

Jeffries did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: El-Sayed downplays antisemitism concerns over rhetoric, says people 'should be uncomfortable' over Gaza
item.description: Michigan Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed dismissed fears that his criticism of Israel could potentially fuel more antisemitism when asked by The Atlantic.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed downplayed critics' concerns that his comments on Israel could fuel antisemitism during an interview with The Atlantic on Tuesday.

El-Sayed discussed his views on Israel, including his accusations that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is a war criminal and that Israel committed genocide during the war in Gaza.

Staff writer Jonathan Lemire asked El-Sayed what he would say to people who believe these criticisms of Israel "fuel [their] fears of antisemitism." Though El-Sayed emphasized that he does not want to frighten people, he suggested that some of the concerns reflected "discomfort" rather than a threat to safety.

'THE VIEW' CO-HOST CONFRONTS ABDUL EL-SAYED ON HIS RESPONSE TO ATTACK ON JEWISH SYNAGOGUE

"I'm sorry for your fear," El-Sayed answered. "Obviously, I don't want to do anything that drives your fear. At the end of the day, there's a difference between safety, or lack of safety, and comfort. If what I'm saying is making you uncomfortable, you should be uncomfortable with injustice perpetrated on other people. You should be uncomfortable with that. I don't want anything we do to make anybody unsafe, to put them in harm's way."

He continued, "But addressing the safety question and the discomfort question are two different things. Because if it is your sense of your discomfort and/or fear of safety that has to keep me quiet while I watch 70,000 people get killed, their homes annihilated, their hospitals destroyed, their universities decimated, and I can't critique that, then I think what you're telling me is that their humanity matters less than yours, and I'm not going to be OK with that."

ABDUL EL-SAYED HITS BACK AT ISRAEL QUESTIONS, SUGGESTS HIS NAME AND FAITH ARE BEHIND PRESS SCRUTINY

When asked what he believes Israel should be as a nation, El-Sayed answered that the country should uphold "equal rights" but appeared to take issue with the nation being associated solely with the Jewish faith.

"I believe that Israel ought to be a country that upholds equal rights for all of its citizens, equal rights for all its citizens, does not identify itself with a culture or a faith, and that dignifies the rights of those citizens to live free under its laws. That’s, again, the question of peace, dignity and self-determination," El-Sayed said.

NANCY PELOSI CALLS MAMDANI, EL-SAYED'S PAST COMMENTS ON ISRAEL 'CONCERNING' AND 'WRONG'

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's team for comment.

El-Sayed has been criticized for his past views on Israel, particularly his hesitation to answer whether he believes Israel has a right to exist.

Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, condemned El-Sayed's comments as "outrageous and hateful" and accused him of criticizing efforts to fight Hamas, the terrorist organization.

"He claims he makes people 'uncomfortable' because he calls it an 'injustice' to destroy the Hamas tunnels, and rescue civilians from torture, sexual assault and murder," Menken told Fox News Digital.

But again, this is a veteran we’re talking about with Lawrence. So, what is the sixth-year franchise quarterback doing himself?

"They got a good Texas bacon cheesesteak [melt], which is good and I get sometimes. They got a Texas bacon chicken [melt], like grilled chicken on Texas [toast]. That one’s really good. I won’t get all into it."

No, Trevor, whenever you want to get into Waffle House talk, we’re here for it.

Perhaps Lawrence will be back at that North Florida Waffle House post-playoffs to celebrate a victory. The Jaguars are on a three-game winning streak heading into Week 11, and at 7-2, they are running away with the AFC South division lead. The Houston Texans are the closest at only 3-6.

In turn, Lawrence and the Jaguars are looking at a home playoff game, but they’re gunning for the top seed in the AFC to ensure they will be playing at home throughout the playoffs until Super Bowl LXI in Los Angeles.

Lawrence won’t be eating Waffle House next week for Thanksgiving, but he will be enjoying some home-cooked family recipes, including the Lawrence’s sweet potato casserole.

But as much as the holiday season is about enjoying time with family and friends, it’s also about giving back. Lawrence did so alongside TikTok chef Jack Macuso at Feeding Northeast Florida, a Jacksonville-based food bank, partner of Feeding America.

The FedEx Air & Ground NFL Awards Program isn’t just fun for players like Lawrence, but it’s committed to tackling food insecurity in collaboration with Feeding America, which led the Jaguars quarterback to put together meal kits stocked with ingredients to make that casserole and more.

"Having the chance to work with FedEx is pretty awesome," Lawrence said. "They’ve been the delivery sponsor for the NFL the last 27 years. They’ve had the FedEx Air and Ground Awards for 24 years and now being in the NFL going on six years, I’m seeing more and more about this award. I was just saying I didn’t realize until probably last year that every time a player wins, FedEx donates money to Feeding America that goes to local communities in the city that player is in. So, I think that part of it is really cool. When I had the opportunity to do this I was really excited.

"I think just having the chance to give back to our community here in Jacksonville and shed some more light on what FedEx is doing, what Feeding America is doing, was really cool."
